a novel class of PARI deletions, located at least 30 to 530 kb downstream of the SHOX gene, is associated with LWD.
we have identified a novel class of PARI deletions in LWD that do not affect SHOX and that these deletions account for 15% in our cohort.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of LWD and the identification of a novel class of deletions downstream of the SHOX locus in patients with LWD.

the molecular genetics of Leri-Weil dyschondroostesis, a rare genetic disorder that affects the skeletal growth of the limbs and the height of patients, and which is caused by mutations in the gene SHOX.
the identification of new genetic causes for short stature and Madelung deformity, which will allow us to improve the molecular diagnosis of LWD, Langer mesomelics and idiopathic short stature.

the SHOX gene is the most important gene for short stature in the pseudoautosomal regions of the human genome.

the SHOX gene is involved in a wide range of phenotypes, and the identification of the molecular basis of these phenotypes will help us to understand the complex mechanisms that regulate the skeletal growth.
